| BB26091701 (found 17 Sep 2026, BUILD session, while building the Creator Studio wizard) | **A `select` field can never carry its choices: `FieldDef` has no `options`, so the wizard's select control always renders empty** | `app/api/src/generate/archetype.rs`'s `FieldDef` declares `field_type`, `required`, `section` and `keys`, but no `options`. `"select"` is in the declared field vocabulary and the JS engine's own wizard reads `field.options`, so the Rust side simply cannot express a select's choices. The Creator Studio wizard (`BB26091204`) renders a `<select>` for the type and reads `options` off the schema — against today's engine that control can only ever show "Select…" and nothing else. Add `options: Option<&'static [&'static str]>` to `FieldDef` and to `FIELD_DEFAULTS`, and surface it in the schema endpoint's JSON. | ⬜ Queued — found while building `BB26091204` | **Not fixed in `BB26091204`'s own session, deliberately.** Adding a field to `FieldDef` breaks every archetype entry that spells its fields out in full rather than using `..FIELD_DEFAULTS` — there are about ten of those (`section: Some("Header"), keys: None` and similar), and they would each need the new field added. That is a mechanical change, but a mechanical change across ten call sites with **no compiler available** is exactly the shape of edit that looks right and is not: no Rust builds on this machine at all (`BH26091501`). It is one small, confident change once `cargo check` runs again. **No archetype in `_common` uses `select` today**, so nothing is visibly broken right now. That is why this is a real gap rather than an urgent one: the first archetype that wants a dropdown discovers it, and by then the wizard looks like the thing at fault. |
| BB26091702 (found 17 Sep 2026, BUILD session, while building the Creator Studio wizard) | **`ValidationResult` carries no field name, so per-field error binding rests on parsing an English sentence** | `archetype.rs`'s `ValidationResult` is `{ valid: bool, errors: Vec<String> }`, and every archetype builds those strings as `format!("missing required field: {f}")`. There is nowhere to put the field name as data. `BB26091204` requires validation errors to bind to their own control rather than surfacing as one opaque failure, so the wizard currently recovers the field by regex over that sentence (`normalizeErrors()` in `app/web/lib/archetypes.ts`). It works, and it keeps an error it cannot attribute rather than dropping it — but the binding breaks silently the day anyone rewords an error message, which is the sort of change nobody expects to be load-bearing. Change `errors` to carry a field name alongside the message (a small struct, or a `(field, message)` pair), have the archetypes emit it, and have the schema/preview/generate endpoints return `errors: [{field, message}]`. The wizard already reads that shape. | ⬜ Queued — found while building `BB26091204` | The wizard's string parsing should stay after this lands, as a fallback — it costs nothing and means an error from an older engine build still reaches the right control. Blocked in practice by the same thing as everything else in `app/api`: no Rust compiles on this machine (`BH26091501`). |
